patch.value: GH-1465: Represent implementer-to-verifier handoff as project context
Assess reported lifecycle ambiguity when completed implementation is released for verification; distinguish a customizable project review queue from active work and preserve handoff evidence.

Reproduce claimed release warning and current status contracts; Evaluate existing custom status/workflow primitives before adding baseline states; Design explicit history-backed handoff and verifier context without marking inactive work in progress; Cover context selection and close/reopen semantics
Projects can express implementation-complete verification queues and accountable handoff without leaving inactive items in progress.

patch.value:
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1465

## Problem

Multi-agent work commonly splits into **implementer → verifier**: an agent finishes, releases its claim, and an orchestrator (or reviewer) verifies the evidence before closing. pm has no lifecycle state for "done, awaiting verification". The allowed statuses are `draft, open, in_progress, blocked, closed, canceled`.

So every implementer ends with:

```text
$ pm release pm-dfrf
status: "in_progress"
warnings[1]: released_unclaimed_in_progress
suggestions[1]: "pm-dfrf remains in_progress and unclaimed. If work is paused, run pm release pm-dfrf --pause to move it to open."
```

The warning is accurate, but in this workflow it is the intended outcome, not an anomaly. In one orchestration session (2026-10-14) two independent agents reported this warning as a probable pm bug. Neither available option fits:
- `--pause` (back to `open`) loses the fact that the work is done.
- `in_progress` + unclaimed reads as abandoned work. A verifier also cannot query its queue: `pm list --status in_progress` mixes active work with handed-off work.

## Repro (2026.10.14)

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$d" && git init -q && pm init >/dev/null
id=$(pm create --type Task --title t --description d --acceptance-criteria a --json | jq -r .id)
pm claim "$id" && pm update "$id" --status in_progress && pm release "$id"
pm update "$id" --status in_review   # Invalid --status value. Allowed: draft, open, in_progress, blocked, closed, canceled
```

## Suggested change

One of the following, or both:
1. A first-class review state, e.g. `in_review` (terminal-adjacent, not counted as active work), with `pm list --status in_review` as the verifier's queue. `pm close` from `in_review` keeps the existing close validation, and `pm item reopen`/`pm update --status in_progress` sends it back with a reason.
2. `pm release <id> --handoff [--to <principal>] [--message <evidence summary>]`. It records the handoff (who, when, to whom, summary) in history, sets the review state (or a `handoff_to` field), and does not emit `released_unclaimed_in_progress`.

Context management benefit: `pm context` could surface "awaiting your verification" separately from "in progress". That is exactly the split an orchestrator needs when 5–10 agents finish at different times.

patch.value: Implementers can hand off unclaimed verification context without marking queued work in progress or requiring a fixed baseline review status; invalid requests preserve ownership and history.

Release accepts a configured non-terminal handoff queue and required evidence, atomically transitions status and clears ownership in one event, honors workflow/ownership policies and rejects conflicting pause through every transport. Public types/contracts/docs and regressions cover the lifecycle.
